The Climate Plan puts Brazil on the path of becoming a sustainable, resilient, safe, fair and prosperous country, with governments, civil society, the private sector and the conscious scientific community, engaged and acting in an integrated way in the face of climate change.

The overall objective of the Climate Plan is to guide, promote, implement and monitor coordinated actions aimed at the transition to an economy with zero net greenhouse gas emissions up to 2050 and the adaptation of human and natural systems to climate change, through short, medium and long-term strategies, in the light of sustainable development and climate justice.
increasing resilience of populations, cities, territories and infrastructure in the face of climate emergency
promote sustainable and resilient production and regular access of the population to healthy foods in adequate quality and quantity
promoting water security, providing water in sufficient quality and quantity for multiple uses, such as supply, production, energy and ecosystems
protect, conserve, restore and strengthen ecosystems and biodiversity, and ensure the provision of ecosystem services
promoting, protecting and recovering the health and well-being of populations, respecting the ways of life of traditional peoples and communities
ensuring energy security in a sustainable and accessible way
promoting socioeconomic development and reducing inequalities
protect cultural heritage and preserve cultural and local heritage practices, facing the risks related to climate change
strengthen the vital role of the ocean and the coastal zone in coping with climate change.

Implement recovery activities of degraded areas that result in both carbon sequestration and reduced deforestation and adaptation of agriculture to climate changes. To this end, the National Program for the Conversion of Degraded Pastages into Agricultural and Sustainable Forest Production Systems (PNCPD) will be strengthened, with emphasis on the adoption and maintenance of sustainable technologies; mapping priority areas for the development of production chains consistent with local and regional socio-bioeconomics; funding for rural producers; and the development of business plans according to the aptitude maps (priority areas and crops/farming practices).

To expand production units using technologies of water recirculation systems (RAS), aquaponia and multitrophic, production of molluscs and seaweed, seeking to meet the foundations of the circular economy. source_text_en: Ensuring the Ways of Life of Traditional Peoples and Communities in the Coastal Zone and Navy in the face of climate change

indicators_en: Number of territories of traditional and collective use formally regulated in coastal and marine.
source_text_en: Increase the number of territories of traditional and collective use formally regulated in the Coastal Zone and Navy until 2030

source_notes_en: To carry out a survey of the formally regulated traditional and collective use territories in the Coastal Zone and Navy and to support the recognition and regularization of new traditional territories in these regions through the Terms of Authorisation for Sustainable Use (TAUS) and the Royal Right of Use Grant Agreements (CCDRU). The TAUs are instruments for granting ownership of Union land in favour of traditional communities, with a view to guaranteeing their livelihood outside the Conservation Units. The CCDRUs are instruments of direct transfer of part or integrality of Sustainable Use Conservation Units (ESEX, RDS and APA) to their beneficiary communities, through the agreement of reciprocal obligations.
source_text_en: Support the recognition of the traditional territories of the Coastal Zone and Navy through the Terms of Authorisation for Sustainable Use (TAUS) and the Royal Right of Use Grant Agreements (CCDRU)

indicators_en: Legal instruments instituted.
source_text_en: Adequate legal instruments to increase the protection of the Coastal Zone of Brazil with a view to climate adaptation until 2030

source_notes_en: The Marine Lands are Union goods and consist of the range of 33 m along the sea coast and the banks of rivers and lakes that suffer the influence of tides, counted from the Middle Preamar Line (average of high tides) according to Decree-Law No. 9.760 of 1946. Currently the destination of these Marine Lands only meets heritage issues, linked to the Union Heritage Secretariat (SPU). What is proposed is that coastal protection to the effects of climate change, such as coastal erosion, salt intrusion, increased frequency and intensity of extreme events, be considered for this destination. Thus, the Marine Lands would be considered as “buffer zones” in order to reduce the impact of these processes, increasing coastal resilience. These areas should have specific rules for building and urbanization, with specific restrictions.
source_text_en: Propose legal instrument to target Marine Lands as a climate adaptation measure to increase coastal zone resilience

source_notes_en: The Safety Range (Art. 1 o, § 3 o, of the Law no 13.240 of 2015) consists of a range of 30 meters wide, which are counted from the end of the beach. It is emphasized that this Safety Range is defined by the current position of the beach and is NOT confused with the Marine Lands, nor with the Permanent Preservation Areas (APPs). The purpose of the Security Strip is property (whether or not it concerns the maintenance of the property of the Union in the stretch), i.e. if the property (land) contained therein is owned by the Union, cannot be disposed of, and the Union cannot give up its property, whatever the instrument of disposal (sale, exchange, donation). The proposal is that the Safety Range be increased and used as a buffer zone against the effects of climate change, with specific restrictions on urbanization, ensuring greater protection to the coastline and increasing resilience.
source_text_en: Propose legal instrument to increase the Coastal Safety Range and target climate adaptation measures to increase resilience of coastal areas
